original_question: Prove that the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation is non-integrable under at least one reasonable notion of infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian integrability.
target_in_paper: Section 10.1, Problem 26: "Prove the non-integrability of the 2D Euler equation." This is the paper's official formulation of the issue your draft is trying to capture. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the correct target PDE (the 2D incompressible Euler equation), the correct qualitative objective (non-integrability), and the key nearby clarification from the paper that it is enough to disprove at least one notion of infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian integrability rather than all such notions. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated: the paper's Euler equation is posed on a fixed domain M or, more generally, on a Riemannian manifold M; here one specializes to the two-dimensional case. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The PDE itself should be written explicitly, together with boundary behavior: ∂_t v + v·∇v = -∇p, div v = 0, with v tangent to ∂M when a boundary is present, and p defined only up to an additive constant. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The Hamiltonian framework should be included: g = Vect_μ(M) is the Lie algebra of divergence-free vector fields, and its regular dual is identified with g* ≅ Ω^1(M)/dΩ^0(M). ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
The Hamiltonian should be named explicitly as the kinetic energy E(v) = (1/2)||v||^2_{L^2(M)}. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The paper stresses that the infinitely many enstrophy invariants are Casimir functionals: they specify the coadjoint orbit but do not by themselves describe the dynamics on that orbit, so they should not be treated as sufficient evidence of integrability. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The draft's phrase "reasonable notion" is looser than the paper's wording. The paper says there are several, not necessarily equivalent, definitions of integrability in infinite dimensions, and the goal is to show failure of at least one of them. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The nearby discussion also says that neither infinitely many conserved quantities nor the ordinary Euler-Poincare Lax form should be counted as good indicators of integrability; in particular, no spectral-parameter Lax form is known there for 2D Euler. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

Items such as ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restrictions, nilpotency conditions, and quantifiers of the form "for all sufficiently large m" do not belong to this paper's formulation and should not be imported into the refined question. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
refined_question: Let M be a two-dimensional domain or Riemannian manifold equipped with an area form μ, and consider the incompressible Euler equation for a divergence-free velocity field v tangent to ∂M when ∂M ≠ ∅: ∂_t v + ∇_v v = -grad p (equivalently, in the Euclidean-domain notation of (1.1), ∂_t v + v·∇v = -∇p, div v = 0). View this equation in Arnold's Hamiltonian framework, where g = Vect_μ(M), g* ≅ Ω^1(M)/dΩ^0(M), and the Hamiltonian is the kinetic energy E(v) = (1/2)||v||^2_{L^2(M)}. Prove that this infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system is non-integrable by showing that the 2D Euler equation fails at least one of the several (not necessarily equivalent) definitions of integrability in infinite dimensions; the issue to settle is genuine dynamical integrability on a coadjoint orbit, not merely the existence of infinitely many enstrophy Casimirs or the generic Euler-Poincare Lax form. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 10.1 rather than a broader neighboring topic. This paper is an open-problems survey, and the nearest official formulation is Problem 26. Section 1 provides the exact Euler equation and boundary convention, Section 10 gives the Lie-Poisson Hamiltonian formulation, and the sentences immediately following Problem 26 explain the intended scope: one should prove failure of at least one infinite-dimensional integrability notion, while not confusing Casimir/enstrophy invariants or the generic Euler-Poincare Lax representation with true integrability. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
